sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first. secrets.py runs in main at process start before the HTTP server comes up, so readiness (GET /healthz) can't pass until the load is done.
sonnet.q2: It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 s apart, then logs names (never values) and exits non-zero, so it never goes ready. Rollout halts (one pod at a time, maxUnavailable 0, new pod must pass /healthz before an old one stops) while old replicas keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background refresher re-reads all three every 5 min after startup; if a version id changed it swaps that entry in one assignment (old or new pair, never a mix) and logs '<name> now at version <id>'. If the read fails (whole vault or one name), it keeps the last good value for what couldn't be read, updates the rest, warns (name + error only), and retries next tick without exiting or going unready.
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-memory, per-process dict of name -> (value, version id) (the only copy). Values must never go to disk, env vars or logs (version ids may be logged).
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*, used by the 4 prod replicas). Write: only security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod.
sonnet.q6: The old keys remain in git history for two years and history won't be rewritten, and pre-migration images still have them baked in. Rotating the keys at each vendor and revoking the old ones (after all replicas show the new versions) makes the old values useless.
sonnet.q7: The clients call secrets.get(name) on every outgoing vendor call and put the result in the Authorization header, rather than copying the key in __init__, so a refreshed key is used starting with the next request, no restart.
sonnet.q8: Check the health endpoint (/healthz secret_versions) on every replica (all 4) and confirm all show the new version id, waiting about 10 minutes (refresh every 5 min); only then does security on-call revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access/permissions and test them; 2) copy keys into the store (prod by security on-call, dev sandbox keys by engineers); 3) one merge switching the app to read from the store and removing the api_key lines from app.yaml (same merge); 4) after the rolling deploy and check in step 8, rotate keys at the providers (payments, then mailer, then geo), revoking old ones last.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store's dev path orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), because make run sets APP_ENV=dev, using the developer's own login.
sonnet.q11: It never starts on a partial set. It retries the whole load 3 times, 2 s apart, then logs the names (not values) and exits with a non-zero code.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security hasn't decided whether there will be a regular schedule or how often; the plan only does the one-time rotation.
